application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A TypeScript HTTP fetch wrapper that adds JSON handling, retries, timeouts, hooks, and normalized errors on top of native or node-fetch based fetch implementations.
application.purpose: Provide a more ergonomic and resilient HTTP client ($fetch/ofetch) for browsers and Node.js.

applicationFacts: The library exposes $fetch and ofetch created via createFetch, with platform-specific wiring in src/index.ts (browser/global fetch) and src/node.ts (Node.js).
Retry defaults differ by method: payload methods do not retry by default while others retry once; retries apply to status codes in retryStatusCodes or a custom list.
Active aborts are not retried automatically; timeouts are implemented via AbortController with a TimeoutError.
Errors thrown by onError are created via createFetchError and include request, options, response, and status accessors.
Response bodies are parsed by detectResponseType unless parseResponse or responseType overrides it; JSON parsing uses destr.
The build config emits declarations and CJS output for src/index and src/node entries.
Call graph within createFetch shows self-recursion via $fetchRaw-related calls and calls to onError, which in turn calls isPayloadMethod and createFetchError.
unknowns: The exact purpose of the self-referencing CALLS relation on src/fetch.ts#createFetch is unclear from the graph alone; the source suggests calls occur through $fetchRaw, which is not a separate graph entity.
Entities such as $fetchRaw, the inner hook-wrapped functions, and test-level functions other than abortHandle are not in the technical graph and were not annotated.
The business context of the library's consumers beyond general HTTP usage is not stated in the source.
